entities.name: Maintain a static widget type registry
entities.shallStatement: The system SHALL maintain a registry of available widget types, each entry containing at minimum: a unique identifier, a display name, a short description, a default grid size (w × h), and a reference to the React component that renders it.

entities.name: Expose registry entries for display in the Add Widget panel
entities.shallStatement: The system SHALL provide the full list of registered widget types to the Add Widget panel UI so they can be presented to the user.

entities.name: Support instantiation of a registered widget type
entities.shallStatement: The system SHALL be able to create a new widget instance from a registry entry, assigning it a unique instance ID and its default grid size.

entities.name: Support extension with new widget types without grid changes
entities.shallStatement: The system SHALL allow new widget types to be registered by adding an entry to the registry array without requiring changes to any grid or layout logic.

entities.name: Notify user when grid is full and block addition
entities.shallStatement: The system SHALL check for available grid space before adding a widget. If no free cell block exists for the widget's default size, the system SHALL display a notification and SHALL NOT add the widget.

entities.name: Provide a remove control on each widget
entities.shallStatement: The system SHALL provide a remove control on each widget

entities.name: Request confirmation before removing a widget
entities.shallStatement: The system SHALL present a confirmation prompt when the user activates the remove control on a widget. The widget SHALL only be removed if the user confirms.

entities.name: Cancel removal without change
entities.shallStatement: The system SHALL dismiss the confirmation prompt and leave the widget on the dashboard when the user cancels the removal.

entities.name: Scaffold the React + TypeScript project with Vite (`npm create vite@latest . -- --template react-ts`)
Install core dependencies: `react-grid-layout`, `@types/react-grid-layout`
Install UI utility dependencies: a toast/notification library (e.g., `react-hot-toast`) for error and reset notifications
Configure TypeScript `tsconfig.json` and Vite `vite.config.ts` for path aliases and strict mode
Set up basic CSS reset and global styles; import `react-grid-layout/css/styles.css` and `react-grid-layout/css/resizable.css`
Define the `WidgetRegistryEntry` TypeScript interface (`id`, `displayName`, `description`, `defaultSize: {w, h}`, `component`)
Create the static `WIDGET_REGISTRY` array in `src/registry/widgetRegistry.ts` with at least three starter widget types (e.g., StatsCard, ChartWidget, TableWidget)
Implement each starter widget component as a simple placeholder React component under `src/widgets/`
Export a `getWidgetComponent(id)` helper that resolves a registry entry to its React component
Define the `WidgetInstance` type (`instanceId`, `typeId`, `x`, `y`, `w`, `h`) and `DashboardLayout` type (`layoutVersion`, `widgets: WidgetInstance[]`) in `src/types/layout.ts`
Define the `DEFAULT_LAYOUT` constant in `src/registry/defaultLayout.ts` with one instance of each starter widget type at sensible positions

Implement `loadLayout(): DashboardLayout` in `src/persistence/layoutStorage.ts` — reads `rdd_layout` from localStorage, wraps parse in try/catch, falls back to `DEFAULT_LAYOUT` on missing or corrupt data, checks `layoutVersion` for compatibility
Implement `saveLayout(layout: DashboardLayout): void` — serialises layout to JSON and writes to `localStorage` under `rdd_layout`

Implement the `useDashboardLayout` custom hook in `src/hooks/useDashboardLayout.ts` — initialises state via lazy `useState(() => loadLayout())`, exposes `layout`, `moveWidget`, `addWidget`, `removeWidget`, and calls `saveLayout` on every mutation
Add version-mismatch detection in `loadLayout`: if `layoutVersion` doesn't match `CURRENT_LAYOUT_VERSION`, clear storage and return `DEFAULT_LAYOUT`
Show toast notification when fallback to default layout is triggered due to corruption or version mismatch
Create `src/components/DashboardGrid.tsx` — renders `<ReactGridLayout>` with 12 columns, `draggableHandle=".widget-drag-handle"`, and maps `layout.widgets` to grid items
Wire `onLayoutChange` callback in `DashboardGrid` to call `moveWidget` from `useDashboardLayout`, updating positions after each drag
Style the `react-grid-layout__placeholder` CSS class with a dashed border and shaded background to clearly distinguish the drop target
Add a CSS modifier class (e.g., `.rgl-placeholder--invalid`) applied when the grid is full during a drag, giving the placeholder a red tint
Ensure grid items snap back automatically via `react-grid-layout` when released outside the grid canvas

Create `src/components/WidgetCard.tsx` — a card wrapper that renders a header with the widget title, a drag handle grip icon (`.widget-drag-handle`), a remove "×" button, and a body area for the widget component
Style the `.widget-drag-handle` with a grab cursor and grip icon; ensure it is clearly visible in the card header
Apply "lifted" CSS styling (reduced opacity + elevated box-shadow) to the card being dragged, using the `isDragging` state from `react-grid-layout`
Ensure pointer events on the widget body do NOT initiate a drag (only the `.widget-drag-handle` region starts a drag)
Verify the built-in `react-grid-layout` placeholder updates in real time as the pointer moves between cells during a drag
Implement a `isGridFull(layout, newWidget)` utility in `src/utils/gridUtils.ts` that checks if any free (x, y) slot exists for the given widget size
Conditionally apply the `.rgl-placeholder--invalid` class to the placeholder when `isGridFull` returns true during an active drag
Show a brief shake animation or toast when a drop is rejected (grid full) to communicate the failure
Confirm placeholder is removed and grid returns to normal display state immediately after any drop (valid or cancelled)
Create `src/components/AddWidgetDrawer.tsx` — a slide-in drawer component that lists all entries from `WIDGET_REGISTRY` with their `displayName` and `description`
Add an "Add Widget +" button to the dashboard toolbar that toggles the `AddWidgetDrawer` open/closed
Implement widget selection in the drawer: clicking a registry item calls `addWidget(typeId)` from `useDashboardLayout` and closes the drawer

Implement `addWidget` in `useDashboardLayout`: uses `isGridFull` to check space; if space exists, finds first free cell, creates a new `WidgetInstance` with a `uuid`, appends to layout, and calls `saveLayout`
Close the drawer without changes when the user presses Escape or clicks outside the drawer
Show a toast notification ("Dashboard is full — remove a widget to add a new one") and block the add when `isGridFull` returns true
Wire the "×" button in `WidgetCard` to open an inline confirmation popover
Implement the inline confirmation popover with "Remove" and "Cancel" buttons; render it anchored to the "×" button
On confirmation, call `removeWidget(instanceId)` from `useDashboardLayout` — filters the widget from layout, calls `saveLayout`
On cancel, dismiss the popover and leave the widget unchanged on the dashboard
Create `src/App.tsx` — instantiates `useDashboardLayout`, renders the toolbar (with "Add Widget" button) and `<DashboardGrid>`, passes layout and handlers as props
Render `<WidgetCard>` for each `WidgetInstance` inside `DashboardGrid`, passing the resolved component from `getWidgetComponent(typeId)`
Mount `<Toaster>` (or equivalent) in `App.tsx` for toast notifications
Verify end-to-end: load app → layout restores → drag widget → layout persists → reload → layout matches
Style the dashboard toolbar with an "Add Widget +" button aligned to the top-right
Style widget cards with consistent padding, border radius, and a visually distinct header strip containing the drag handle and remove button
Style the `AddWidgetDrawer` as a right-side slide-in panel with smooth open/close animation
Add responsive grid breakpoints (e.g., lg/md/sm) using `react-grid-layout`'s `Responsive` wrapper if needed
Ensure the drag handle grip icon uses an appropriate cursor (`grab` / `grabbing`) to clearly communicate draggability
